title: dev-team verdict.json
description: Shape of .dev-team/verdict.json, the machine-readable summary the dev-team-review skill writes alongside its human-readable .dev-team/VERIFICATION.md report (see skills/dev-team-review/references/verdict-and-report-protocol.md, 'VERIFICATION.md structure'). It exists so a CI step can gate a build on the review's outcome (exit non-zero on a FAIL verdict) without having to parse the markdown report. This file is JSON, which has no comment syntax of its own, so every field's reason for existing and who reads it is recorded here in its 'description' instead of in '//' comments that would make the file invalid JSON.
$comment: File: schemas/verdict.schema.json. Validates tests/fixtures/verdict.sample.json (see tests/scripts.bats) and is meant to be run in CI against every verdict.json a dev-team-review run produces, using check-jsonschema (pip install check-jsonschema; see .github/workflows/plugin-audit.yml). Written for issue #41 (moving dev-team's own files into .dev-team/), which is also why the 'dev-team' marker field below exists on this ledger the same way it exists on every markdown one. Note on 'additionalProperties: false' just below: it is set on purpose, so that a field added under a new or misspelled name (e.g. 'verified_count' instead of 'verified') fails this check loudly and immediately, in CI, rather than being silently accepted and only noticed much later by a person reading the JSON by eye. A genuinely new field is added here, with its own description, in the same change that starts emitting it — this schema is not meant to be a ceiling on the format, only a guard against silent drift.

dev-team.description: The dev-team ownership marker for this file, in the form every dev-team ledger carries (see conventions.md, 'Where the plugin writes, and the ownership rule'). Its purpose is NOT versioning by itself — it is the proof that a JSON file found at .dev-team/verdict.json is this plugin's own, not a same-named file left there by something else, so that a reader (or a future ownership check) can tell the difference without guessing.

overall.description: The headline verdict for the whole review, gated by the worst claim that matters rather than an average of all claims (see verdict-and-report-protocol.md, 'Overall verdict rule'). PASS: every claim that matters is VERIFIED and the integration check passed. PASS_WITH_GAPS: nothing critical failed, but there are real gaps (HOLLOW tests, DRIFTED records, non-critical FAILED claims). FAIL: a critical claim failed, or the app does not actually run end to end. A CI gate normally fails the build only on FAIL.

checked.description: How many claims this review pass actually looked at. Read alongside 'claims' (whose length should normally equal this number) as a cross-check that nothing was silently dropped between counting and listing.

verified.description: Count of claims whose verdict is VERIFIED: freshly re-checked and found true.

failed.description: Count of claims whose verdict is FAILED: freshly re-checked and found false. Any FAILED claim marked critical severity is what drives 'overall' to FAIL.

drifted.description: Count of claims whose verdict is DRIFTED: the record says one thing, and the fresh evidence shows the real state has moved on from it (for example, a security finding recorded as fixed-verified that the record now contradicts).

hollow.description: Count of claims whose verdict is HOLLOW: something that passes on paper (a test, a check) but was found not to actually exercise what it claims to — for example a coverage number that never touches the code path it is supposed to cover.

unverifiable.description: Count of claims whose verdict is UNVERIFIABLE: the reviewer could not get fresh evidence either way (no environment to run it in, no way to reproduce it), so the claim is neither confirmed nor denied.

integration.description: Result of the clean-room integration check: built and run from a fresh checkout, does the primary user task actually work end to end. This is deliberately separate from the per-claim counts above, because a project can have every individual claim VERIFIED and still not actually run — this field is what catches that case, and a 'fail' here forces 'overall' to FAIL regardless of the claim counts.

regressions.description: IDs of claims that were VERIFIED in the previous VERIFICATION.md report for this project but are failing again now (see verdict-and-report-protocol.md, 'Regression delta'). Optional: a first-ever review for a project has no prior report to compare against, so there is nothing to list. An empty array means the comparison ran and found no regressions, which is a different, stronger statement than the field being absent.

items.description: A verification-claim id in this plugin's id scheme (see conventions.md, 'ID prefixes') — always 'V-' followed by at least three digits, e.g. V-001 or V-104.

improvement_findings.description: Count of improvement findings (id prefix I-0xx) raised alongside the verdict: things that work correctly but could be made leaner or faster. These do not affect 'overall' — a project can PASS while still carrying improvement findings — and only feed the optional fix phase when the review's 'improve' setting is on (see verdict-and-report-protocol.md, 'Fix phase'). Optional because a quick-depth review may skip the efficiency pass entirely.

claims.description: One entry per claim this review pass checked — the machine-readable form of the 'Per-claim results' table in VERIFICATION.md. Every id counted in 'checked' above should appear exactly once here.

items.description: A single claim's result. Deliberately NOT locked down with additionalProperties:false the way the top-level object is — a claim may carry extra fields (a short description of what was claimed, a link to the fresh evidence) that are useful to a human reading the JSON directly but are not needed by an automated CI gate, so they are allowed rather than rejected.

id.description: This claim's verification-record id, e.g. V-001. Matches an id in the project's own VERIFICATION.md 'Per-claim results' table.

verdict.description: This one claim's result. See the top-level 'verified'/'failed'/'drifted'/'hollow'/'unverifiable' fields for what each word means; the counts above are simply how many claims carry each of these five values.

severity.description: How much it would matter if this claim were wrong — not how bad the verdict already is. 'n/a' is for claims (for example a fully VERIFIED, non-critical one) where severity was never a live question. A FAILED or DRIFTED claim at 'critical' severity is what forces the overall verdict to FAIL.

confidence.description: How sure the verifier is of this particular verdict, independent of severity — for example a DRIFTED verdict reached from a single ambiguous log line would be 'low' confidence even if the claim itself is critical.
